It is run by the Rhodes Trust and looks for academically excellent people who show leadership, strong character and a commitment to serving others.

The 2027 cohort is for candidates starting at Oxford in October 2027. Scholars normally study for two years on eligible full-time postgraduate programmes, and certain approved pathways have extra conditions.
eligibility:
Open to eligible candidates from participating Rhodes constituencies around the world. Requirements differ by constituency and may include:
Citizenship or residency rules.
Age criteria.
Strong academic achievement.
Eligibility for the chosen full-time postgraduate course at Oxford.
Evidence of leadership, initiative, character and commitment to service.
English-language level that meets Oxford University's requirements.
Use the official eligibility checker and read the candidate information document for your constituency before applying.
benefits:
Payment of Oxford University course fees.
An annual stipend to help cover living costs, including accommodation.
Stipend of £21,060 for 2026-27, paid in monthly instalments. The rate may change for 2027-28.
Funding for the standard scholarship tenure, subject to the official conditions.
documents:

Application materials required by your constituency.
Referee details (referees also have their own deadline).
Evidence of academic achievement.
English-language evidence that meets Oxford's requirements.
Oxford postgraduate course application, if you are selected.
steps:
Identify the correct Rhodes constituency for your circumstances
Review the eligibility criteria and deadlines for that constituency
Prepare the required application materials and referee information
Submit your application through the official process
If selected, apply to your Oxford postgraduate course and meet its admission requirements

overview:
The Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA) 2027 Visiting Fellowship supports early-career international researchers who want to do research on climate change and environmental challenges at a French research institution.

It is funded by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, in partnership with the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space, and run by Campus France.

Eligible research themes:
1. Earth system sciences
2. Climate change and sustainability sciences
3. Energy transition
4. Societal challenges related to environmental issues
5. Human, animal and environmental health under the One Health approach

Innovative projects using advanced technologies in these areas get particular consideration. One Health projects must genuinely address the links between human health, animal health and ecosystems. Projects focused only on medicine or human health, with no environmental or animal-health side, are not eligible.
eligibility:
Hold a doctoral degree awarded less than five years before the deadline, with the thesis defended between December 2021 and December 2026 inclusive.
Foreign nationality (French nationals are not eligible).
Applying for international research mobility to France.
Not living and working in France at the time of applying.
Never received a MOPGA fellowship before.
The eligibility period may be extended in some maternity-leave cases, with official evidence.
benefits:
€2,500 per month for 12 months.
One-time €500 settling-in allowance.
Health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance.
Supplementary health insurance once registered with the French social security system.
Chance to work with French research laboratories and institutions.
Not covered: international travel to France. The fellowship cannot be renewed and cannot be combined with a French employment contract or other individual funding from a French government body.
documents:
CV with publications (maximum 4 pages).
Doctoral degree certificate or official proof of the PhD defence.
CV of your proposed scientific supervisor at the French host laboratory (maximum 2 pages).
Support letter from the supervisor, co-signed by the laboratory director or with the required commitment letter.
One to three recommendation letters.
Copy of a passport or national identity document.
Research project description: objectives, methodology, timeline, relevance to MOPGA and expected impact.
steps:
Find a suitable French research laboratory and scientific supervisor
Write a research proposal that fits one of the eligible themes
Prepare the required documents and recommendation letters
Complete the online application on the official Campus France platform
Submit before 15 December 2026
notes:
Applications can be written in English or French.

Applications open: 15 September 2026.
Deadline: 15 December 2026.
Expected results: May to June 2027.
Expected arrival in France: September to December 2027.

title: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS) for Undergraduate Degrees 2027
org: NIIED | Ministry of Education, Republic of Korea
desc: Fully funded Korean government scholarship for international students to study a bachelor's or associate degree in South Korea, normally after one year of Korean language training. 286 scholars will be selected.
funding: Tuition + monthly allowance + economy airfare + one year of Korean language training
deadline: 30 September 2026 (Embassy Track); November 2026 (University Track, per each university's own schedule)
overview:
The Global Korea Scholarship for Undergraduate Degrees (GKS-U) is run by the National Institute for International Education (NIIED) under Korea's Ministry of Education. It invites international students to study at universities in Korea and normally includes one year of Korean language training before the degree starts.

For 2027, 286 scholars will be selected. You must choose one of two tracks:

Embassy Track (156 bachelor's scholars): apply online through the Study in Korea website. The Korean embassy does the first selection, NIIED the second, and universities the third. Programs: General, Overseas Koreans and Adoptees, and R-GKS. You can choose up to 3 universities (at least one Type B), or up to 2 Type B universities for R-GKS.

University Track (100 UIC and 30 associate degree scholars): apply directly to one participating university and one department, using that university's own method and deadline.

You cannot apply through both tracks at the same time. An Embassy Track applicant who fails the first round may apply once through the University Track if that university's deadline is still open.
eligibility:
Citizen of a country designated by NIIED for the program (the UIC program is open to all countries).
Both parents or legal guardians must hold citizenship of a country other than Korea. Korean dual citizens are not eligible.
Under 25 years old: born after 1 March 2002.
Graduated, or expected to graduate by 31 December 2026, from high school (or an associate degree for a bachelor's). People who already hold a bachelor's degree cannot apply.
Grades from the previous program: 80% or higher, OR top 20% of the class, OR CGPA of at least 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0.
Good physical and mental health for the full program.
Generally not eligible: graduates of Korean high schools, previous Korean government degree scholarship recipients, and anyone who withdrew or was disqualified from GKS in the last 3 years.
benefits:
Tuition: NIIED covers up to KRW 5 million, and the university covers the rest plus the admission fee.
Korean language program fee: KRW 5.2 million per year.
Economy-class airfare, based on actual cost.
Monthly allowance: KRW 13,560,000 per year during the Korean language program and KRW 14,400,000 per year during the degree. It is all-inclusive and covers living costs, accommodation, health insurance, the TOPIK fee, settlement and degree completion grants.
Scholars already living in Korea at the final announcement do not receive entry airfare.
Amounts can be changed by NIIED.
documents:
Forms: Application Form (in English), Personal Statement, Study Plan, Recommendation Letter, GKS Applicant Agreement, Personal Medical Assessment, and Consent to Collect and Use Personal Information.
Proof of your and your parents' citizenship and family relationship.
High school graduation (or expected graduation) certificate and full transcript.
For bachelor's applicants with an associate degree: that certificate and transcript.
TOPIK or English score report, if you have one (optional).
Up to five awards or certificates from high school onward.
Passport copy.
If you pass the first round, certificates need an apostille or consular confirmation, and a certified translation if not in English or Korean.
steps:
Check that you meet the eligibility rules and choose either the Embassy Track or the University Track
Download the University Information file from the official Study in Korea notice and pick only universities and departments listed there
Prepare the forms, certificates, personal statement, study plan and one recommendation letter
Embassy Track: apply online at www.studyinkorea.go.kr during your embassy's application period
University Track: apply directly to one university using its own 2027 GKS-U notice, deadline and delivery method
If you pass the first round, submit signed originals and authenticated certificates as instructed
Take part in the interview and follow the results on the Study in Korea website
notes:
Deadlines:
Embassy Track: 30 September 2026, 18:00 Korean time. This has closed, and some embassies set their own dates, so check the notice from the embassy in your country.
University Track: November 2026, according to each university's own schedule. Check your chosen university's website for its exact date.

Expected schedule:

Second round by NIIED: late November 2026.
Third round (Embassy Track only): by 23 December 2026.
Final announcement: expected 7 January 2027.

TOPIK level 3, 4 and 5+ add 3%, 4% and 5% to the score, and science and engineering applicants get an extra 5%. All scholars in the language program must reach TOPIK level 3 to start the degree, and some departments require level 4.

desc: Paid five-month traineeships at the European Parliament for graduates, in areas such as European policy, law, communication, finance, administration, IT and multilingualism.
funding: Monthly grant (amount depends on location and allowances)
overview:
The European Parliament offers paid Schuman Traineeships to help graduates gain practical experience and learn how European institutions work. Trainees work in areas such as European policy, law, communication, finance, administration, IT, multilingualism, infrastructure and logistics.

The session runs for five months, from 1 March to 31 July 2027, in Brussels, Luxembourg, Strasbourg or the Parliament's Liaison Offices in EU Member States.
eligibility:
At least 18 years old.
A full university degree, or the specific qualifications for a vocational traineeship.
Thorough knowledge of one official EU language and very good knowledge of a second.
An eligible criminal record.
No more than two months of previous work or traineeship experience in an EU institution, body or agency.
Meet the other programme rules, including limits on recent study visits to the Parliament Secretariat.

India and other non-EU countries: the programme mainly targets nationals of EU Member States and EU accession or candidate countries. A limited number of traineeships may be open to nationals of other countries, so check each vacancy. Eligibility is not guaranteed.
benefits:
A monthly grant, depending on the location and allowances.
Practical experience inside the European Parliament.
Chance to build professional skills while learning about European policy and decision-making.
The exact grant amount should be confirmed on the official website.
documents:
Online application through the Parliament's application portal (up to three traineeships).
If shortlisted: supporting documents to verify your eligibility.
steps:
Visit the official European Parliament traineeships page
Open the application portal and look through the available positions
Choose and apply for up to three traineeships
Submit before the deadline
If shortlisted, provide the supporting documents requested
notes:
Deadline for the March to July 2027 session: 31 October 2026. Applications must be sent in the official application period. Spontaneous applications are not accepted.

Confirm the vacancy details, grant amount and nationality rules on the official website before applying.

title: NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship 2027-2028
location: Mandatory in-person summer internship at an eligible NVIDIA research office
desc: Up to US$60,000 for outstanding PhD researchers whose work advances accelerated computing, with NVIDIA mentorship and a required in-person summer internship. International PhD students can apply.
funding: Up to US$60,000 per award, paid through your university toward stipend, tuition and mandatory fees
overview:
The NVIDIA Graduate Fellowship Program supports outstanding PhD researchers whose work advances accelerated computing and related technologies. It offers research funding, collaboration with NVIDIA researchers, mentorship and a mandatory in-person summer internship.

Research areas include artificial intelligence and machine learning; computer science and computer engineering; system architecture and electrical engineering; robotics and autonomous vehicles; computer graphics and computational imaging; networking, security and privacy; high-performance computing and parallel programming; and healthcare and life-science computing.

Applicants should explain how their research connects to NVIDIA's areas and could influence the design, performance or use of future GPUs.
eligibility:
Completed your first year of PhD-level study before applying.
Researching computer science, computer engineering, system architecture, electrical engineering or a related field.
Actively working on your PhD thesis research.
Stay enrolled as a full-time PhD student for the nine-month award year.
Available for the required in-person summer internship before the fellowship year.
Not a full-time NVIDIA employee or an immediate family member of one.
International PhD students can apply. Published internship locations include the United States, Canada, Germany, Sweden, Finland, Switzerland, Israel, Taiwan and Singapore.
benefits:
Up to US$60,000 in research funding.
Chance to work with NVIDIA researchers.
Research mentorship and technical support.
An in-person summer internship at an eligible NVIDIA research office.
A chance to present research at GTC San Jose.
The award goes through your university to support eligible stipend, tuition and mandatory fees. The amount depends on your actual eligible costs and is not necessarily paid directly to you.
documents:
Research proposal of up to two pages (excluding the bibliography).
CV or resume with contact details.
Two or three recommendation letters, including at least one from your thesis adviser or a professor.
Confirmation that you are available for the required summer internship.
steps:
Visit NVIDIA's official Graduate Fellowship page
Review the eligibility rules and research areas
Prepare your research proposal and CV
Invite your recommenders through the application portal
Confirm your availability for the in-person summer internship
Submit and make sure all recommendation letters arrive before the deadline
notes:
Deadline: 30 October 2026, including recommendation letters. This is very soon, so contact your recommenders now.

Read the official guidelines on the proposal, university funding arrangements and the mandatory internship before applying.

title: Heinrich Böll Foundation Washington DC Internships
org: Heinrich Böll Foundation | Washington, DC office
desc: Three to six month internships in policy research, international relations, democracy, climate and digital policy at the Heinrich Böll Foundation in Washington. Monthly stipend of $700 for full-time interns.
funding: $700/month stipend (full-time) + 5 paid vacation days per 3 months + most visa application costs may be covered
overview:
The Heinrich Böll Foundation's Washington, DC office offers internships for students and recent graduates interested in policy research, international relations, democracy, climate change and digital policy. The foundation works on policy reform and political dialogue, with a focus on democracy, human rights, environmental protection, climate policy and peaceful conflict resolution.

Internship areas:
1. Climate and Energy: environmental policy and international climate finance.
2. Foreign Policy and Democracy: foreign and security policy, democracy and international affairs.
3. Global Transition: global development policy and digital policy.

Interns may help with research, communications, events and visitor programmes. They must also complete a capstone project, such as a policy paper, an interview with a policy expert, an explanatory video script, or a series of blog posts or opinion pieces.
eligibility:
At least two years of university-level experience.
Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's programme, or finished a Bachelor's degree less than one year before applying.
Experience in at least one of the foundation's programme areas.
A genuine interest in the foundation's mission and values.
Competent English. German is not required.
Mid-career professionals and people who already have a Master's or PhD will not be accepted for these internships.
International applicants should check the specific vacancy for eligibility, work authorisation and visa arrangements.
benefits:
Monthly stipend of $700 for full-time internships.
Five paid vacation days for every three months of a full-time internship.
Most visa application costs may be covered by the foundation.
Washington, DC is expensive, and the foundation encourages applicants to seek extra financial support if needed, so do not assume the stipend covers all living costs.
Part-time arrangements may be considered case by case.
documents:
Application materials following standard U.S. practice (for example a CV and cover letter), as the vacancy asks.
Apply only through BambooHR. Applications sent any other way are not considered.

Visit the official careers portal
Look through the vacancies and their requirements
Pick a suitable position and check its application deadline
Prepare your materials following standard U.S. application practice
Submit through BambooHR

desc: An on-site software engineering internship in Tokyo offering technical training, mentorship, and practical projects in full-stack or front-end development. The program is unpaid but provides eligible participants with a living-expense subsidy and specified additional benefits.

Participants receive guidance from experienced engineers and work on practical training assignments involving web application development, cloud technologies, testing, and infrastructure.

The program offers two pathways: Full-Stack Engineering and Front-End Engineering. Knowledge of Linux, macOS, or another Unix-like environment is expected.

Visa-related guidance and pre-arrival assistance.

Applicants must demonstrate leadership experience gained through employment or civil society engagement.

Applicants must meet the academic and tuition-fee liability requirements and follow the university admissions process.

Full tuition fee coverage paid directly to the Swedish university under the scholarship terms.

Monthly living allowance of SEK 12,000.

Membership in the SI Network for Global Professionals.

Access to professional networking, knowledge exchange, and development opportunities.

level: PhD students and early- to mid-career professionals, including researchers, public health practitioners, healthcare professionals, and policy-makers
title: WHO Summer School 2027: Systems Thinking and Innovation for Public Health
org: WHO Regional Office for Europe, Université Côte d’Azur WHO Collaborating Centre, and Ulysseus European University
desc: A four-day, in-person summer school for PhD students and early- to mid-career professionals interested in systems thinking, noncommunicable disease prevention, healthy ageing, and evidence-based public health policy. funding: No course fee. Lunch and coffee breaks are included each day, along with a welcome dinner on 21 July 2027. International travel, local transport, accommodation, visa expenses, travel insurance, and other personal costs are not covered.
overview:
The WHO Summer School 2027 on Systems Thinking and Innovation for the Prevention of Noncommunicable Diseases and a Healthy Ageing Population in the WHO European Region is a professional training programme in Nice, France.

Organized by the WHO Regional Office for Europe in collaboration with the WHO Collaborating Centre at Université Côte d’Azur and Ulysseus European University, the programme aims to strengthen participants' ability to understand complex public health challenges and develop evidence-based policy approaches.

Participants will learn from WHO specialists and international experts through lectures, interactive workshops, practical exercises, and real-world scenarios. Topics include systems thinking, noncommunicable disease prevention, healthy ageing, public health innovation, policy scenarios, artificial intelligence in public health, and translating research into policy.

The programme is limited to 30 participants and is delivered in person in English. A certificate of participation is provided.

Potential applicants include postgraduate students, researchers, public health practitioners, healthcare professionals, policy-makers, public health innovation professionals, and specialists in healthy ageing and noncommunicable disease prevention.

Applicants should have a relevant academic or professional background and demonstrate interest in the programme's themes.

Selection considerations include professional experience, educational background, research or professional experience, the quality and relevance of the personal statement, and potential for future collaboration.

benefits:
Free participation with no course fee.

Expert-led training in systems thinking, public health innovation, and evidence-based policy development.

Interactive workshops, practical exercises, and real-world case studies.

Skills in noncommunicable disease prevention and healthy ageing.

Exposure to tools for systems analysis, policy scenarios, and decision-making.

Opportunities to connect research findings with public health policy.

Networking with international researchers and professionals.

Certificate of participation.

Lunch and coffee breaks each day, plus a welcome dinner on 21 July 2027.

Review the selection criteria and prepare the required application materials.

Arrange for two referees to submit recommendation letters directly to UNU. 5. Submit the online application and required documents before the deadline. 6. Follow any interview or assessment instructions.
notes: Application deadline: November 1, 2026, at 11:59 PM Japan Standard Time. Expected internship dates: March 1 to August 27, 2027. Applicants must disclose their actual or projected funding while in Tokyo. The stipend is conditional and only partially subsidizes living expenses.

title: UN DPoA Midterm Review Journalism Fellowship 2027
org: United Nations Office of the High Representative for the Least Developed Countries, Landlocked Developing Countries and Small Island Developing States (UN-OHRLLS)
desc: The DPoA Midterm Review Journalism Fellowship supports journalists from UN-designated Least Developed Countries to attend and report on the Midterm Review of the Doha Programme of Action in Doha, Qatar. The program aims to connect global sustainable development commitments with the priorities and experiences of people in LDCs.
funding: Selected fellows are expected to receive round-trip economy-class airfare, a daily subsistence allowance for accommodation and meals under applicable UN rules, pre-conference orientation where applicable, fellowship briefings, and networking opportunities. Final support is subject to the award letter and applicable requirements.
overview: The fellowship plans to select 10 journalists to report on the Doha Programme of Action Midterm Review, scheduled for March 25–27, 2027. Reporting themes include poverty reduction, education, health, science and technology, structural transformation, trade, climate resilience, and international partnerships.
eligibility: Applicants must be at least 18 years old, be nationals of one of the 44 UN-designated Least Developed Countries, and be professional staff or freelance journalists whose work is regularly published or broadcast by a recognized media outlet. At least two years of professional journalism experience, an interest in sustainable development, and availability for the fellowship activities are required.
benefits: Round-trip economy-class travel to Doha; daily subsistence allowance for accommodation and meals under applicable UN rules; possible pre-conference orientation; fellowship briefings; and networking with development stakeholders and journalists.
documents: A professional biography of no more than 300 words; two published journalism work samples, including at least one development-related piece; and a reporting proposal of no more than 400 words describing planned story angles, audience relevance, DPoA implementation, formats, and intended publication outlets.
steps: 1. Visit the official UN-OHRLLS fellowship page. 2. Confirm nationality and professional eligibility. 3. Prepare the biography, two published work samples, and reporting proposal. 4. Complete the official online application. 5. Submit all required materials before the deadline. 6. If selected, participate in the fellowship activities and produce the required reporting outputs.
notes: Application deadline: November 30, 2026. The event takes place March 25–27, 2027. Fellows are expected to produce at least three substantive journalism outputs and share publication links by April 30, 2027. India is not on the eligible LDC list. Selection does not guarantee conference accreditation, a visa, or travel clearance. No application fee is stated.

title: CaCTüS Summer Research Internship 2027 in Germany
org: Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics, Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, and Tübingen AI Center
desc: The CaCTüS Summer Research Internship offers hands-on research experience at the intersection of artificial intelligence, biological intelligence, neuroscience, and cognition. Interns work on research projects under the supervision of scientists at participating laboratories in Tübingen.
funding: The opportunity announcement describes approximately €1,350 monthly salary, accommodation arranged by the program, health insurance support, and compensation for eligible travel costs. Visa application fees and related embassy expenses may not be covered.
overview: CaCTüS stands for Computation and Cognition Tübingen Summer Internship. The three-month program is open to eligible applicants from all countries. Research projects may involve AI, machine learning, theoretical neuroscience, computational modeling, cognitive science, computational psychiatry, behavioral experiments, data analysis, and scientific software development.
eligibility: Applicants should have a relevant academic background, a strong interest in scientific research, good English skills, and availability for the full internship period. Bachelor's students must have completed at least four semesters before the internship begins. Master's students and eligible Bachelor's or Master's graduates may apply if they have not started a PhD by the internship. Applicants may be asked to explain circumstances limiting their access to advanced research opportunities.
benefits: Approximately €1,350 monthly salary; accommodation arranged by the program; health insurance support; eligible travel-cost compensation; research mentorship; hands-on scientific experience; and professional development opportunities.
documents: CV of up to two pages; motivational statement describing research interests, relevant experience, and selected projects; university academic transcripts; degree certificates where available; and an optional reference letter.
steps: 1. Visit the official CaCTüS program website. 2. Review eligibility and research projects. 3. Prepare the CV, transcripts, and motivational statement. 4. Select research projects matching your interests. 5. Complete the online application and upload the required documents. 6. Submit before the deadline. 7. Attend a virtual interview if shortlisted.
notes: Application deadline: November 16, 2026. Interviews are expected in January 2027 and acceptance notifications in February 2027. Internship dates: July 1 to September 30, 2027. Verify salary, accommodation, insurance, travel reimbursement, and project availability through the official program information.

title: EPFL E³ Summer Research Internship 2027
org: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), School of Engineering
desc: The EPFL Excellence in Engineering (E³) Program gives international Bachelor's and Master's students the opportunity to conduct summer research in engineering, science, and technology laboratories. Participants are matched with host laboratories according to their academic background and research interests.
funding: Monthly living allowance of CHF 1,800 for host laboratories in Lausanne, Sion, and Fribourg, or CHF 2,500 for host laboratories in Geneva and Neuchâtel. Travel costs may be reimbursed upon request and approval by the host laboratory. Participants arrange their own accommodation.
overview: The E³ program offers research placements lasting two to three months during the May–October 2027 period. Research areas include AI, computer science, electrical engineering, robotics, bioengineering, materials science, microengineering, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, energy, sustainability, and data science.
eligibility: Applicants must be enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at the time of application and remain enrolled throughout the internship. Bachelor's students must have successfully completed at least two years of study by the time of application. Applicants should have a relevant engineering, science, or technology background and strong academic performance. PhD students are not eligible. Students at certain partner institutions may need to apply through a separate EPFL program.
benefits: Monthly living allowance of CHF 1,800 or CHF 2,500 depending on host-laboratory location; possible travel reimbursement with host-laboratory approval; research experience; and the opportunity to work with EPFL research teams.
documents: CV; complete academic transcripts; motivation letter or statement of purpose; and passport or national ID. Applicants may select up to three research topics and indicate up to three preferred host laboratories. Documents should be PDFs. English translations of transcripts may be supplied alongside originals where required.
steps: 1. Visit the official EPFL E³ website. 2. Review eligibility, FAQs, research topics, and host laboratories. 3. Prepare the CV, transcripts, motivation letter, and identity document. 4. Complete the online application and select research interests. 5. Review the application carefully and submit before the deadline. 6. Attend an online interview if invited.
notes: Application deadline: November 1, 2026, at 23:55 Swiss local time. The internship period is May–October 2027, with placements lasting two to three months. Applications cannot be modified after submission. Applicants must maintain student status throughout the internship. Verify the current host-laboratory and partner-institution rules.

title: IWA & Grundfos Youth Action for SDG 6 Fellowship 2027–2028
location: Online, United Kingdom, Denmark, and Malaysia
desc: The IWA & Grundfos Youth Action for SDG 6 Fellowship supports young water professionals developing practical innovations for water-related challenges. The program combines professional development, online activities, peer learning, expert engagement, and selected international water-sector events.
funding: For required fellowship travel and in-person activities, support is expected to include economy-class airfare, single-occupancy accommodation, meals, ground transportation, travel insurance, and visa application fee coverage. The fellowship does not provide direct grants or investment to implement participants' projects.
overview: The 2027–2028 fellowship focuses on advancing Sustainable Development Goal 6: clean water and sanitation. Activities may include monthly online meetings, capacity-building sessions, peer-learning groups, innovation showcases, engagement with IWA and Grundfos experts, an initial gathering in the United Kingdom and Denmark, and participation in the 2028 IWA World Water Congress & Exhibition in Malaysia.
eligibility: Applicants must be aged 18–35 by the end of December 2028, have an active IWA Young Water Professional membership or qualify through the eligible Grundfos employee route, and be engaged in the water sector. benefits: Professional development; capacity-building; peer learning; expert engagement; access to IWA and Grundfos networks; opportunities to present innovations; and expected coverage of travel, accommodation, meals, local transport, travel insurance, and visa application fees for required in-person activities.
documents: CV of up to two pages; motivation letter of up to two pages; reference letter of up to one page, ideally from an IWA member; and innovation proposal of up to two pages. steps: 1. Read the official fellowship announcement. 2. Confirm age, membership or employee-route eligibility, and program conditions. 3. Prepare the CV, motivation letter, reference letter, and innovation proposal. 4. IWA members should access the application through IWA Connect Plus using active membership credentials. 5. Eligible Grundfos employees should use the dedicated internal application route. 6. Submit in English before the deadline. 7. Attend an interview if shortlisted.
notes: Application deadline: November 5, 2026. Interviews are tentatively expected in late November and selections in mid-December 2026. Fellowship activities run from February 2027 to December 2028. Applicants should have an innovation in development; an idea alone is not sufficient. Confirm membership requirements and travel arrangements on the official website.
